- Kate Crawford

- Brian Medina
 
Installing a guardrail system on a parapet roof can be a challenging and risky task, but there are some steps you can take to ensure safety and compliance with OSHA standards. Here are some tips based on the web search results:
 
- Before you start, you should assess the roof conditions and identify the hazards, such as skylights, roof hatches, or unprotected edges. [You should also plan the layout of the guardrail system and determine the materials and tools you will need](https://www.bing.com/aclk?ld=e89f81D-6ZDV1g4Ok5lRv8aTVUCUxsHL-QMOwOI7XmzlblS5HWfNT6Jdkn33dMJe_C_k1w81eJdqa999eQznK_t7QHkcA_EoKszWi2ugjUCcpdG_9PbFio2L46RElGLUeLrBgzrrvW6jxMS1sOFl5Lt-b04uFQOyBOaY-69TqFto7p7PU5&&rlid=7e064a5a3842110af73e2f739bc7b4d3)[1](https://www.legat.com/osha-roofing-safety-guidelines-worker-safety-on-low-slope-roofs/). - You should wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), such as heavy-duty gloves, steel toe boots, non-slip soles, and a climbing helmet. [You should also use a personal fall protection system, such as a harness, a lanyard, and an anchor point, to prevent or arrest a fall](http://about:blank#)[2](https://simplifiedsafety.com/blog/how-to-install-guardrail-safely/). - You should choose a guardrail system that is suitable for your roof type and meets OSHA height and strength requirements. [For example, you can use clamps that attach to the parapet, horizontal base plates that rest on the roof surface, or toeboards that prevent tools from falling over the edge](http://about:blank#)[3](https://www.fallproof.com/blog/guardrails-for-rooftop-hatches-skylights-and-roof-edges/). - You should install the guardrail system from a safe position, such as an aerial lift or a designated area with a warning line. You should avoid working near the edge without proper fall protection. [You should also follow the manufacturer’s instructions and secure all the components properly](http://about:blank#)[2](https://simplifiedsafety.com/blog/how-to-install-guardrail-safely/)[4](https://simplifiedsafety.com/blog/how-to-stay-safe-when-installing-railing/). - You should inspect the guardrail system regularly and maintain it in good condition. You should also train your workers on how to use it safely and correctly. [You should document your installation and inspection procedures and keep records of any incidents or injuries](http://about:blank#)[1](https://www.legat.com/osha-roofing-safety-guidelines-worker-safety-on-low-slope-roofs/)[5](https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/docs/2014-108/pdfs/2014-108.pdf).
       
According to the web search results, the minimum height of a wall or guardrail on a roof per OSHA depends on the type of work and the roof conditions. However, the general requirements are as follows:
 
- [For guardrail systems, the top edge height of top rails, or equivalent guardrail system members, should be](https://www.bing.com/aclk?ld=e8ACwdpf4E4aQGmutFo6KliDVUCUz7ud0QR4ujomjcMslLW7t-GAE6Kq8N3e4DvsmRgD63pdh3_YtdL_-HGtl2DMr5TF0RCqn1zkmCYJzCNA7tnWiPm8R3t9G-ZvNQB_Li33v9IliP-01DJ4zn8Q37wTy7gpe-7glN0Wvf1KmfRJv0IvIF&&rlid=0a96d7fc73c11881bf69b2d5d5bf3847) **42 inches (107 cm)**, plus or minus 3 inches (8 cm), above the walking-working surface[1](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.29). [The top edge height may exceed 45 inches (114 cm), provided the guardrail system meets all other criteria of OSHA standards](https://www.bing.com/aclk?ld=e8ACwdpf4E4aQGmutFo6KliDVUCUz7ud0QR4ujomjcMslLW7t-GAE6Kq8N3e4DvsmRgD63pdh3_YtdL_-HGtl2DMr5TF0RCqn1zkmCYJzCNA7tnWiPm8R3t9G-ZvNQB_Li33v9IliP-01DJ4zn8Q37wTy7gpe-7glN0Wvf1KmfRJv0IvIF&&rlid=0a96d7fc73c11881bf69b2d5d5bf3847)[1](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.29). - [For walls or parapets, they should be at least](https://www.bing.com/aclk?ld=e8ACwdpf4E4aQGmutFo6KliDVUCUz7ud0QR4ujomjcMslLW7t-GAE6Kq8N3e4DvsmRgD63pdh3_YtdL_-HGtl2DMr5TF0RCqn1zkmCYJzCNA7tnWiPm8R3t9G-ZvNQB_Li33v9IliP-01DJ4zn8Q37wTy7gpe-7glN0Wvf1KmfRJv0IvIF&&rlid=0a96d7fc73c11881bf69b2d5d5bf3847) **21 inches (53 cm)** high to serve as a guardrail system[1](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.29). [If the wall or parapet is lower than 21 inches, then additional fall protection measures are required, such as midrails, screens, mesh, or intermediate vertical members](https://www.bing.com/aclk?ld=e8ACwdpf4E4aQGmutFo6KliDVUCUz7ud0QR4ujomjcMslLW7t-GAE6Kq8N3e4DvsmRgD63pdh3_YtdL_-HGtl2DMr5TF0RCqn1zkmCYJzCNA7tnWiPm8R3t9G-ZvNQB_Li33v9IliP-01DJ4zn8Q37wTy7gpe-7glN0Wvf1KmfRJv0IvIF&&rlid=0a96d7fc73c11881bf69b2d5d5bf3847)[1](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.29). - [For warning line systems, they should be erected not less than](http://about:blank#) **6 feet (1.8 m)** from the roof edge for work that is both temporary and infrequent, or not less than **15 feet (4.6 m)** for other work[1](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.29).
